what: The constructor discovers positive loc and visited facts from semantic fact names, identifies the unique depot as the location without a visited predicate, and stores the exact SAS variable/value references. It parses grounded visit, visit-via-depot, and return-to-depot operator names once and obtains their metric costs to build directed routing matrices. For each state it reads all propositions once, identifies the current location and unvisited customers, constructs a nearest-neighbour relaxed completion ending at the depot, and improves that path with up to three best customer-relocation passes. Customer transitions use the cheaper available direct or via-depot grounded cost. The resulting finite path cost is returned as the remaining-cost estimate.
why: CVRP states are naturally summarized by the current location and unvisited customer set, while grounded operators expose the directed routing costs robustly without parsing translator-generated numeric expressions. A completed route estimate is more informative for search than a simple unvisited-count or independent-edge bound. Nearest-neighbour construction is inexpensive at the representative instance sizes, and limited relocation search repairs many greedy ordering mistakes while keeping evaluation quadratic. Via-depot operator costs represent route resets without requiring fragile extraction of capacity, demands, or vehicle limits.
